title: Pergamon Museum
visualBrief: Pergamon Museum: complete connected mapped three-wing museum with open west court, limestone gallery wings with tall recessed glazing and pilasters, heavy cornices, hipped/stepped roof forms, central stepped entrance wall and roof lanterns, lower east service alcove and the mapped glazed entrance vestibule. This asset represents the mapped pre-renovation entrance configuration. The2026 picture informs surviving stone facades; construction pits, scaffolding, temporary signs and a future fourth wing are not reconstructed. Keep James-Simon-Galerie, Neues Museum, Bode Museum, surrounding colonnades, canal/quays and all unrelated buildings as context.

sourceFacts.horizontalBasis: Q157298 and named PMTiles way313659704/native35184685748536 establish the museum. Integral ways231549083/084/085/086/087 identify main hall, south wing, east service alcove, vestibule and north wing. Internal+X follows the mapped south-southeast front edge between wing ends; +Z points west-southwest through the open courtyard toward Kupfergraben. Heading0 with orientation baked into east/south geometry. Do not remove independent James-Simon-Galerie way194422265, Neues Museum way18578139, Bode Museum relation4211594 or neighboring colonnades.
sourceFacts.architecturalHeights: Mapped30m central hall,25m wings,10m vestibule and15m generic parent are unqualified overall height controls. Reconstructed central wall24.2m with stepped roof/lanterns to30m, wing walls22m with hipped roofs to25m, east alcove14.2m plus roof to15m. Pilaster/window inventories, recess depth, cornice profiles and hidden roof plant are picture-led approximations. The large glass vestibule follows the2004 image and retained map, not the partly rebuilt2026 entrance. Furnished galleries, antiquities, copied lettering/artwork and future construction are omitted.
